method: Amish rows are the Young Center's 2026 state/county/settlement table, parsed verbatim (705 settlements; the district total of 3,229 matches the Young Center's published US total). A settlement the source lists under several counties (including cross-state counties such as 'St. Joseph MI') gets one row per county with the same name; the source does not split districts by county, so 'districts' is the settlement total divided evenly across its counties (fractional where needed) and 'settlement_districts' keeps the unsplit total. County FIPS were matched by state and county name against the Census 2023 gazetteer; four source spellings were corrected (Lousia->Louisa IA, Onedia->Oneida NY, Connejos->Conejos CO, Lyons->Lyon KS) and Van Wert, listed without a state suffix under Indiana's Adams County settlement, was assigned to Ohio. One source row (Cold Spring, Jefferson WI) has no district figure, so districts is null. Old Order / horse-and-buggy Mennonite rows are a PARTIAL list: the Young Center publishes these settlements only as state-level counts by group (about 60 US settlements across 8 groups), so the 33 county rows here were assembled from a 2014 JAPAS Kentucky table, a 2019 JAPAS New York profile, GAMEO and Wikipedia; where a source named only a town, the county is the town's county. Mennonite 'districts' are null (congregation counts were not available at settlement level). Beachy/Amish-Mennonite and other car-driving groups are excluded.
